name: write
description: Run one INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE with bound parameters ($1, $2, ...) and an intent. The guard in the database records old and new rows. DDL, multiple statements, data-changing WITH, COPY and functions outside the allowlist are refused. A write of 11 to 50 rows, or any DELETE, is held: the result is APPROVAL_REQUIRED with approveCommand, a short command for the person to run in their terminal that opens the approval page (give them that rather than the long approvalUrl, which breaks when copied). Once the person approves with their passkey, call write again with the same arguments plus approvalId (and approval, if the person gave you the code).

sql.description: Exactly one INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE statement.

intent.description: Why this change is made, in a sentence a person can review.

runId.description: The run this write belongs to, from run_start. A one-write run is started when absent.

approvalId.description: Apply a held write: the approvalId from APPROVAL_REQUIRED. Repeat the same sql, params, intent and runId.

approval.description: The person's signed approval code (basalt-approval.1.…), if the person gave it to you. The engine submits it to Postgres, which checks the passkey signature; needs approvalId.

returning.description: Rows from a RETURNING clause, keyed by column name.
